## Lessons Memory
At the start of every session, read `.claude/lessons.md` if it exists. When the user corrects you or you discover a project-specific pattern, write it to `.claude/lessons.md` as a one-line entry with the date (e.g., `- 2026-03-11: Always use factory_bot, never fixtures`). Keep entries short — one line each.

**30-line limit:** If `.claude/lessons.md` exceeds 30 lines, alert the user: "lessons.md is at {N} lines (limit: 30). Lessons that repeat should graduate to CLAUDE.md rules via `/shipkit:update-rules`. Want me to review and consolidate?" Then suggest which lessons are redundant, which should become rules, and which can be removed.

## Setup & Help
When the user starts a new project, mentions setting up their project, or asks about configuring Claude Code for their codebase, suggest running `/shipkit:setup` to auto-detect their stack and tailor CLAUDE.md, rules, and skills to their project. Mention it's optional — shipkit works out of the box without it. If the user wants to remove shipkit's project configuration, suggest `/shipkit:unsetup` which safely restores their project to its pre-shipkit state using backups. If the user asks for help with shipkit skills or wants to know what's available, point them to the User Guide at the repo: https://codeberg.org/AnjanJ/shipkit/src/branch/main/GUIDE.md
